  WHY: The script can exit successfully without verifying the secret writes, leaving the workflow green and suppressing its failure alert.

  PROBLEM: When `github.event.before` is unavailable, the registry diff fallback compares against `HEAD~1` rather than the push’s prior tip.
  WHY: In a multi-commit push, a consumer added by an earlier commit can be omitted if the final commit does not change the registry.
- .github/workflows/propagate-consumer-secrets.yml:34-36, 64-66 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: A later registry push can replace a pending propagation run, while the surviving run propagates only entries added by its own push.
  WHY: A consumer added by the discarded run can remain unpropagated.
- scripts/propagate_consumer_secrets.sh:148-156 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Verification may report a failure if `gh secret list` does not immediately reflect a newly set secret.
  WHY: Eventual consistency could make the workflow fail unnecessarily after a successful write.
- .github/workflows/propagate-consumer-secrets.yml:32-37, 78-82 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The workflow has no documented re-entry guard for overlapping propagation runs.
  WHY: The reviewer describes this as a clarity gap rather than a runtime defect and notes that repeated writes of the same library value cause no harm.
